This time the toys get two animation clips. The prompt on screen is an illustrative reconstruction, not a saved transcript.

beats.role_note: walker B01 — what was built and what the film explains. The correction is the misconception the body dismantles: the clips run on the physics tick (state_t), not the display clock.
beats.narration_text: Tin Knockout got two clips: a wind key that turns while a fighter rewinds, and a jab that commits. Both run on the physics clock, not the display's: every tick, each clip is put where the fighter's state timer says. Tests prove the timing. Whether the motion reads, only eyes can say.

beats.role_note: The game, both clips, their routes, what loops and what commits (TEST-REPORT "The two clips", CHANGE-BRIEF §1), with held frames from the film capture.
beats.narration_text: The game: two tin toys box on wind-up springs, and every attack spends wind. Clip A, wind key cycle, is the cycle. Its route: a Sprite two D sliced into eight frames, driven by an animation player's frame track. It loops: eight keys at eight frames a second, one turn a second, while the fighter rewinds. Clip B, jab action, is the committing action. Its route: a cutout rig keyed as resource text, two named pivots, Body Pivot and Key Bob. It commits: twenty-one frames at sixty, no loop, and nothing the player presses can stop it.

Nothing checks that path when the file loads.

beats.role_note: Why a renamed property fails silently: mutation M1 (evidence/a7/mutations/README.md, its logs; TEST-REPORT A7-5).
beats.narration_text: Rename that property by two swapped letters, rotatoin, and the engine says nothing. The game ran with the rotation track inert, and no warning. Only the read-back caught it: track problems, Body Pivot has no property rotatoin. Eight of forty-eight checks failed. The structure test caught it again on the real Bolt and Rivet. A track's path is a promise the loader never checks.

beats.narration_text: Second question: who writes each node? Lines sixty-seven to seventy-three name one writer per rig node. Facing Pivot, the body sprite and Key Mount: apply pose. beats.narration_text: The structure test reads every script and lists every assignment to a rig node, by function. Re-run for this film: after setup, the only writes are apply pose's Facing Pivot scale, and Key Mount's position and visibility. Body Pivot and Key Bob are never written by code, and nothing writes the key's frame. On every jab tick, the pose equals the clip's own value at the state timer: largest gap, zero.

beats.narration_text: In play. The jab lands on its fifth tick. For the next five ticks, hitstop holds the state timer, and the clip holds frame five with it: the logged clip position stays at point zero eight three three. Then measured by Tharun, in a window running free: the display at about one hundred twenty-nine frames a second, physics at sixty ticks, and the clip against the state timer, on two hundred seventy-nine jab ticks: largest gap, zero. The picture trails gameplay by under one tick.

beats.role_note: Question 4, feel in frames: CHANGE-BRIEF §4 phase table at 60 fps beside evidence/a7/jab_action_keys.md.
beats.narration_text: Fourth question: feel, in frames. Tharun's phase table, at sixty frames a second: startup, frames zero to four; active, the box live, five to ten; recovery, eleven to twenty; idle on twenty-one. Beside it, each key's time in the resource: a key at every boundary. Frame three, the coil: minus six pixels. Frame five, the lunge: plus fourteen, held to ten. Frame eleven, the release. The times are stored as thirty-two-bit floats, so the read-back compares them within half a frame.

beats.narration_text: The strip is a fixture: the real fighter alone at x two oh seven over the light stretch, the jab on frame ten, captured by Tharun at sixty. Frame thirteen, the coil. Fifteen, the box opens: the lunge, the largest move in the clip. Twenty, the last active frame, the same pose. Twenty-one, recovery begins. Thirty-one, idle. Tharun's first look, written before Claude read the strip: the fighter's whole body leans back first, then pushes forward with the punch arm already extended as part of the jab picture, holds briefly, and pulls back to the starting stance.

beats.role_note: The sheet's slicing as built: godot/tools/generate_key_sheets.gd:37-47 (Claude), the recipe from CHANGE-BRIEF §2 (Tharun).
beats.narration_text: The sheet. Tharun's recipe, in Claude's generator script: eight cells of eighty-four by sixty, in one row. Line thirty-nine: cell k is the key turned k times forty-five degrees, its width scaled by the cosine, never below fifteen percent, so the edge stays legible. Line forty-four: cells three to five are mirrored, the back half of the turn. Line forty-seven blits each one, centred, into the sheet.

beats.role_note: The two committed sheets (godot/assets/props/key-*-sheet.png), sliced 8 x 1 with cell numbers; the cell-centre measurement (TEST-REPORT A7-9c); source and licence (ATTRIBUTION.md, SOURCES.md A7).
beats.narration_text: The result: two sheets, six hundred seventy-two by sixty, eight cells by one. Cells two and six are the key edge-on, at the fifteen percent minimum. Measured, every cell is centred at x forty-one and a half or forty-two, of eighty-four, so the key does not wander. The source art is Tharun's key from assignment two, made with SDXL Turbo from his prompt, under the Stability AI Non-Commercial Research Community License. Each sheet is a derivative, made by resizing and mirroring only.

beats.role_note: The frame track that reads the sheet: godot/animations/wind_key_cycle.tres:3-19.
beats.narration_text: The frame track that reads the sheet. Line six: loop mode one, linear. Line seven: a step of one eighth of a second. Line eleven: the path ends at key sprite, colon, frame. Line seventeen: update one, discrete. Frame is an integer, so on continuous updates the track would sweep through every cell in between. Line fifteen: eight keys at k over eight, and none at the length, one second: frame zero is not repeated at the seam.

Each cell holds seven or eight ticks. Watch the wrap from seven to zero, at every turn. Tharun's check, in his words: the key rotation stays continuous across the wrap without a visible jump at the seam.

The prediction: frames twenty-two to thirty step evenly, seven point two down to point eight pixels, still moving on frame thirty.

beats.role_note: Interrupts in startup (e+3), active (e+7) and recovery (e+15) by Rivet's cutlass, and the key turning in REWIND then holding at full wind; same capture.
beats.narration_text: Now the interrupts, timed as the edge test times them: Rivet's cutlass lands on its ninth tick, so it is requested nine ticks before the hit. In startup, on the jab's third tick. In active, on the seventh. In recovery, on the fifteenth. Each time, jab to hurt on the hit tick, and the rig snaps to rest; no pose is left hanging. Last, Bolt holds S at forty wind. The key turns, six clicks to full wind, a turn and a half, then holds, and goes back to frame zero on release.

beats.role_note: What the read-backs proved (counts re-run for this film on a clean copy of a5978c0), the mutations that failed them (TEST-REPORT A7-4, A7-5) and what no headless run can show (CLAUDE.md Headless facts).
beats.narration_text: What the tests proved, re-run for this film on a clean copy. The key cycle's read-back: twenty-six checks, none failed. The jab's: fifty-eight. Structure and state: fifty-seven, at sixty and at thirty. Edges: seventy. Pins: forty-nine. Then the mutations, each in its own worktree. M one, the renamed property: exits eight and two. M two, the cycle's loop mode set to none: two. M three, a frame key of eight, past the sheet: five. The engine printed a plain error there, which the wrapper does not fail on. M four, an empty import cache, passed, as expected, because nothing here is imported. And the limit: a headless run draws nothing, so whether the motion reads is not observable there.

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught (TEST-REPORT A7-11), including the seam bug (A7-9a, evidence/a7/seam/): the structure test before and after the fix.
beats.narration_text: Agent mistakes, caught. Claude's expectations in the pins were wrong twice: the defender's hitstop, and empty's ninety-seven ticks. The structure test's first draft flagged a read as a write. The edge test expected idle before a hit on tick twenty-one; the jab ends and the hit lands on the same tick. And the biggest: Claude's sync clips sought the key backwards across the wrap. The fixture's first log showed seven, one, zero at every wrap after the first, while the suite was green: the structure test stopped at one and a half turns. The fix moves forward. A six-turn regression failed three checks before it, and none after.

beats.narration_text: Where Tharun's eyes overruled Claude's reading. Claude read r0 as a stall, then a snap. Tharun, in play, found the retraction pop on frame twenty-one, which Claude's reading did not flag; his observation drove revision two. His checks, in his words: startup, hold, and return read as distinct moments. Both clips remain readable over both light and dark backgrounds, with clear enough contrast to follow the motion. And in his own account: writing my first look before reading the strip taught me how easy it is to project motion that isn't actually drawn.

beats.role_note: Human and AI contributions as SOURCES.md "Who did what (A7)", shown verbatim; the brief's drafting note (SOURCES.md A7, verbatim); sheet source and licence.
beats.narration_text: Who did what, as SOURCES dot m d records it. Tharun chose both clips, the routes, the sixty-frame phase table with its poses and easing, the eight-frame cycle and its sheet recipe, the authority layout and the interrupt rules, and wrote the two dated revisions. He swapped in the wrapper, approved the step five plan and the seam fix, ran every capture, wrote the first look and both verdicts, and did the human checks and the two-clocks measurement. Claude Code wrote the facts sheet and probes, the sheet generator, both clips, the tests, the wiring and both previews; ran the mutations; found and fixed the seam bug, with approval; read the strips and wrote the predictions; and drafted the docs. The brief was drafted and refined across four review rounds with Claude Code in the terminal.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — checked by numbers / by eye, uncertain (A7-12), one next step; revision shown.
beats.narration_text: The verdict, at revision a five nine seven eight c zero. Checked by numbers: both read-backs, structure, edges and pins at their counts; three mutations caught, and the fourth honestly not, because nothing here is imported. Checked by eye, by Tharun: the seam, the jab in play, registration and both backgrounds; two revisions, both kept. Still uncertain: the jab picture appears five frames before the hitbox, from the art per state, outside the clips; mashing J shows the idle image for one frame between jabs; and in the game a rewind fills within two and a half turns, so five wraps were watched in the fixture. One next step: a startup image, so the arm stays back until the box opens.
